utterances.text: And can you -- you said, I believe, that the vehicle, your vehicle, was allowed inside the gate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you, roughly, remember where your vehicle parked when it went inside the gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we passed through the gate, we parked immediately to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you see, roughly, where you were parked on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was a little bit further off to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I apologise. Let's go back to the last photograph, 1915. Now, if you can, can you take this pen and just put a little bus-like rectangle where your minivan was parked? It should leave a mark.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, and let's -- so did you ever get out of the vehicle when it was parked there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Brano came up to the vehicle, and he just told Zoran to park there, and the two of them went together into this -- how can I explain it? For me, it was some kind of reception area or guard house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you put GH for guardhouse just on the building where you saw these guys go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And tell us what happened next, what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not long after that, Brano and Zoran came out with a military person, and from what I could see of his rank insignia on his chest, he was a lieutenant-colonel. And then another two policemen, military policemen, came out of the building together with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you describe the person that you believed was a lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was quite tall, corpulent, greyish hair. His face had strong features in this area, and he was wearing a uniform of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't have a beard or a moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember any eyeglasses?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember exactly, but I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you've also mentioned two military policemen came with him. How do you -- how did you know that they were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They had the insignia of the military police. I didn't see it right away. I think that one of them had a white cross belt. I can't remember exactly, but I think that he did have a white cross belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing any patch or insignia that said anything on these two people that you've described as military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I only saw that later. I couldn't see it there. I saw it later, once they came out of the vehicles at the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the persons you saw come out of vehicles at the Branjevo Farm, were they the same two people you saw come out of the guardhouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were the same people, plus this lieutenant-colonel was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm skipping ahead a bit, but what were you able to make from their insignia or from their patch at that time, these people you've said were the military policemen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I could see that they were members of the military police of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What, precisely, do you remember seeing or reading?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can recall exactly reading "military police." As for the rest, I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You have always said "Drina Corps." Do you remember why you concluded Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, because the headquarters of the Drina Corps, I assumed it was in Zvornik, and that's why I always said that that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to the guardhouse, when the two military policemen and the lieutenant-colonel come out. Then describe to us what happens.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were accompanied by Brano Gojkovic and Aleksandar Cvetkovic, they came out together with him. He drove our vehicle. And Brano said that we were going to follow the vehicle in which these two military policemen and the lieutenant-colonel were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me finish up this exhibit. I'm sorry. I of course noticed that as you walked away. We need you just to date it. It's the 4th of May. And put your name on this I think in the -- yeah, down in the right-hand corner is fine.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The whole name or just my initials?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think initials are fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So tell us how it was that you left and who you followed in leaving this area.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not long after they came out of that guardhouse, the lieutenant-colonel and two policemen got into an Opel Cadet car. I remember the colour of the vehicle was olive-green. And Brano said we would follow them, and we took the direction of Bijeljina on the Zvornik-Bijeljina road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember, was there any grey in this colour at all? Can you describe that colour a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "olive-green," that was precisely that olive-green-grey, in fact, like the colour of the uniform that used to be the uniform of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember what style car this was, how many doors it had?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the number of doors exactly, but it was an Opel Cadet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And who led as you left the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The two policemen were up front and the lieutenant-colonel in that car that was ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Roughly how long did you stay at this little compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Ten, twenty minutes, I can't say exactly. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember roughly the time of day it was that you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning. That's all I can say. I cannot tell you the exact hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did these two vehicles go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said before, we took the road that leads from Zvornik to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I forgot to ask you one thing. While you were in that van, did you hear any radio traffic over the Motorola that you remember now, while you were still parked there at the compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We heard over the radio that the Muslims who had left Srebrenica and who were in the woods surrounding Zvornik had captured some police from Doboj and seized one vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So let's get back to the trip. Where did you -- where did you end up stopping on this trip going towards Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped at the farm, which in my estimate was halfway between Zvornik and Bijeljina. I cannot say that this is a precise estimate, but that's my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What did you see when you got to the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we got to the farm, I could see it was a farm. I saw a tractor, trailers, agricultural machinery, and there were people in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not many. Perhaps four, five. I don't know. They were in an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where was the office? Can you describe the building?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The building had one story. It was an old structure. I don't know how to explain. It was a long building, and at the beginning -- at one end, there was an entrance to that office, but I didn't go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did the lieutenant-colonel and the military police make it to this farm with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They brought us there to the farm, and when we arrived, the lieutenant-colonel went into that office. And everybody who was there, who was there before our arrival, left, and only one person remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're talking about the men that were in the military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano talked to the lieutenant-colonel, and when he came back, he said -- in fact, the lieutenant-colonel came back with him, and they said that in a few minutes buses would start arriving, carrying people from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said "they said." Do you remember which person said that buses would be starting to arrive?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, Brano told us, but I believe the lieutenant-colonel was also involved in that talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the people in the uniforms that had previously just left, were you able to make out any patches, insignia, or anything that would indicate to you what unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were told by Mr. Gojkovic that people would be arriving from Srebrenica in buses, what was the next thing you learned?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that civilians from Srebrenica would be coming. That's what he said, civilians, and that they were to be killed that day, which to some of us, me included, appeared unbelievable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were all sorts of exchanges among us, and if -- and Brano said, "If you think that they would not shoot you, give me your rifle and stand in the same line with them."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Shortly after, that lieutenant-colonel and the two policemen got into their car, that same Opel Cadet, and left. I believe they had not yet left the farm when the bus arrived carrying people from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When the buses arrived, I could see that there was a driver and two persons in uniform, the uniform of the VRS, who I suppose accompanied the bus, and then Brano and Golijan approached the bus, talked to those two policemen, and said they would bring out the people from the bus in groups, that we should line up and escort those people to the site which they had designated as the site where they would be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you follow those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they brought out ten persons. We were standing in a line. If I remember well, the first people from that first bus were blindfolded and their hands were tied behind their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then what?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We took those people -- I can't be precise, but I believe it was 100, 200 metres away from the bus, and then we were ordered to shoot at them. They had their backs to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who gave you the order to shoot?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many of you were in the execution squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what kind of weapons were you shooting with?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did everyone follow that order?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what happened after those men were killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the same thing happened. They took people out from the bus in groups, group by group, and the second group followed the first one. Groups were of ten, and they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you take part in all those executions at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long did this go on?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose from 10.00 a.m. until 3.00 or 4.00 p.m. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did any bus drivers have to get involved in this?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after several buses had come and gone, some individuals who were there on the farm started drinking, and Brano had this idea that bus drivers could later be witnesses and that they, too, should kill at least one person each.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what happened after Brano's idea?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: One of the bus drivers was given a rifle by Brano, and he had to shoot one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see any other bus drivers have to shoot anybody?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I know only about that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there a time when any other weapons, besides automatic rifles, were used in this execution?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can't say exactly how much time had elapsed when Aleksandar Cvetkovic said that this execution is proceeding slowly and that they would also start to use the M-84 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a significantly larger-calibre hand-held machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was that used to execute Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was used on two groups of ten, and then a major quarrel amongst us erupted because that machine-gun was a powerful weapon and it just butchered those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the people did not die. They lay on the ground and begged for someone to come and kill them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why wouldn't a machine-gun of that size kill them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose, because I'm not an expert, it had a larger gunpowder charge, and it went through the body. I don't know; I assume that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Did any other troops arrive that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Early in the afternoon, people from Bratunac came.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, how did you conclude they were from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Because Brano said people from Bratunac would be coming. In fact, he recognised people from Bratunac. And because Zoran -- sorry, Aleksandar Cvetkovic recognised some among them. That's how I drew the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many of these men arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Eight or ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Most of them were wearing uniforms of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know what unit they were from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there anything to indicate that any of these men that arrived would have known any of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some of them who knew some Muslims, and some abused the Muslims because they knew them, and one person I recognised on a video spoke quite normally with a person who used to be the butcher in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that, that person that you recognised, in a minute. When you say these men abused the prisoners, can you describe that in more detail? I'm sorry to take us through all that, but it's important.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: What do you want to know? How they abused them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just describe what you mean by "abuse."

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they beat them with their rifle-butts. Some even used some metal bars they found on the farm. Kicked them, punched them, cursed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when did this -- the killing end at the farm that day, roughly what time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was perhaps 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Besides those men from Bratunac, and let me just ask this, anything from their uniforms that you could -- give you any indication where they were from, what unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, I didn't feel at all like looking at them to see what unit they belonged to. I wasn't interested in that because something much worse was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Besides these men from Bratunac arriving, did anyone else arrive that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, towards the end, that lieutenant-colonel came and the two other men who had brought us to that farm in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The ones you described as military policemen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And at about what time did the lieutenant-colonel and the two military policemen return?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon. I don't think the last bus had been finished yet, but that last bus was being done by those people from Bratunac. I already said it could have been 3.00 or 4.00, so sometime around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to go back to the man with the bandana and show you photos you've seen before. If we could go to 65 ter number 1919, which is a video still. All right. Now, this is not a good photograph, but did you see a much clearer picture of this person when you saw the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this photograph that you saw taking part in the killings at Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think -- can you just take the pen, if you could, and just mark an X over the person's head, just so it's absolutely clear which person we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if you could just initial and date this one as well. Again, it's the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to the other one, which is 1918.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any idea when and where was this picture taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is on -- this is Potocari, as they're walking into Potocari on the 12th. It's part of the trial video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can the witness tell us the name of the person he's marked or indicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know this person's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, looking at this photograph, there's a person on the far left of the screen with a bandana. Is this the same person, as far as your recognition is, as the one you saw in the previous photo?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, so this was one of the men at the Branjevo Farm taking part in the executions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this was one of the men from -- that you've identified as being from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I want to now go to 65 ter 1799. This is an aerial image that -- I want the unmarked version, if we can. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think while the witness has used the marked version over the years, it's probably better that we use an unmarked version for these purposes, and if we could just put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While that is being done, is there any objection from any of the Defence teams on using the other photo which has markings on it already and which the witness is familiar with? Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Not with respect to specifically what you said, but we do have an outstanding objection with respect to the markings on the photograph on the top identifying specifically, and that issue still hasn't been resolved as to who put that on the photograph. But with this witness, I don't think it's necessary to repeat that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to the other issue that Mr. Ostojic has raised, I think it's high time you come back with a stipulation or an agreement so that we can have the evidence of Mr. Ruez as soon as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think there's so many markings on that one with the yellow, it might be just easier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Up to you, Mr. McCloskey. I'm not going to interfere in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can just -- let's try with the ELMO, and if we could zero in on that just a little bit more. Okay, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this -- well, this place, first of all?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I do, but this is an aerial photograph, so -- but I do recognise the place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you think you can, could you -- she'll give you a pen, and I think we can mark right on this, right on this photograph. Can you mark the area where the first bus with Muslims in it pulled up?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of a mark should I make?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you can, just a rectangular, like a bus as if, you know, we were putting it there. I know it's hard to get the scale, but ...

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if he could mark 1B on top of that line, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The other buses that arrived throughout the day, did they park in roughly the same place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you -- if you can tell, can you mark with an X where the first group of prisoners were taken to be shot? And I think we need -- we may need to pull out a bit from this close-up shot. Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. You've made an X there. And you've described a building where soldiers were -- the lieutenant-colonel went in. Can you make out from this shot which building that was? Only if you can.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could he put an O next to that line, please, or just below.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think if we can just get an initial and a date, it's break time.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could bring up 65 ter 2804.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you may recall yesterday we spoke briefly of insignias, VRS insignias, and I showed you a grouping of three insignias that had just been pulled up from the internet, and you -- do you recall identifying those insignias for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you saw our -- the interpreter wrote your answers to the questions relating to these insignias; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you start with -- first of all, do you recognise those insignias on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just asked that the smaller insignia above the little plaques be crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And why was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Because I wasn't sure. I know that these were small metal plaques, and I know the first one is major, the second one is lieutenant-colonel and the third one is colonel, but the insignia above, I was not familiar with. But then later I tried to see in a photo, and I could see that generals used these insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So as far as you know, those circular things above these ranks were not used at the time in July, 1995 for these ranks?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I know is that on the 16th, in the morning, when you asked me, "How could you tell he was a lieutenant-colonel," I answered that there was this insignia in the middle indicating that he was a lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where was the insignia that you saw on this lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was on his left side, on the military blouse, shirt he was wearing that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And to be clear, there was no little, round insignia that you saw on his shirt at the time; that's why there's an X through this particular one; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I'm going to jump out of time just to finish the exhibits. There are some still photographs, 65 ter 1975, and these are stills taken from the video of a ceremony in Vlasenica, the Court may remember. It's 65 ter 2034. And if you could just look at these stills briefly. Now, we see on this exhibit four photographs. Do you recognise anyone or any members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment in any of those four photographs?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On A, B and C, I recognise -- I recognise persons from the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which platoon, the Bijeljina or the Vlasenica one?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers from both platoons are there, from Bijeljina and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall being at a ceremony where people were standing like this, I believe, in the late 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. We went there, I myself and some other people from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So let's go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. McCloskey. Just before you showed those photos, you mentioned two 65 ter numbers, and I just wanted to confirm which one that was. You said 1975 and then you said 2034.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. 1975 are the stills, and they were taken from this video of 2034.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back briefly to the Branjevo Farm, and I believe you said at the end of -- near the end of the day, the lieutenant-colonel returned. Can you tell us what happened when the lieutenant-colonel returned with the two military policemen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When he returned, he immediately started saying that in Pilica there is a cultural hall, Dom Kulture, and that there were 500 people there from Srebrenica who were trying to break down the door and who were trying to escape from there, and he said that we needed to go there and execute those people. I, however, and some other people from my unit refused to do that, but the people that came from Bratunac that day, they went with the lieutenant-colonel and the two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you remember what vehicles they left in?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was the same vehicle that the lieutenant-colonel came in, the Opel Cadet. I'm not sure, though. The people from Bratunac came in a Tam, T-a-m, van, I think, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when that group left the farm, what did your group do?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. We prepared our weapons, ammunition. We put that in the van. And Brano said that the lieutenant-colonel said that we were to meet at the bar in Pilica, a coffee bar in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many Muslim men do you estimate were killed that day at the Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: According to my estimate, between 1.000 and 1.200.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you make that estimate?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what I already told you. I'm not quite sure, but it was based on the buses that were arriving. That's how I was able to come to a conclusion. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have a rough number of buses that you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but in my previous testimony and also in my case as well, from 15 to 20, but no one can know how many exactly and what.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you go to Pilica with your group?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know roughly what time of day it is that you finally leave that farm and go over to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was after noon, maybe 3.00, 4.00, 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you drove into the area of Pilica, tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in front of the coffee bar in Pilica, across the road from the coffee bar was the cultural hall, and between the cultural hall and the coffee bar, the road linking Zvornik and Bijeljina passed, and you could see several bodies. I don't know for sure how many, but there were bodies in front of the cultural hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We went where Brano told us that the lieutenant-colonel was supposed to come to meet us. We went to the coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: How do you mean, what did we see? In the bar or what I saw of what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just tell us what you saw, you know, everywhere. Just tell us what you saw as it was happening both in the bar or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Like I already said, it was possible to see from the road where we turned off to go to the coffee bar, and just there was the cultural hall, and you could see bodies in front of the cultural hall already. Also, there was a check-point of the civilian police of Republika Srpska there. Vehicles were passing normally there. There was civilian houses around. There were people. You could hear firing and explosions from the direction of the hall. There were no people in the coffee bar. It was empty. Just the people who worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the police check-point, did you see any civilian police officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. They did not wear civilian clothing, but they were in blue camouflage uniforms, which I knew was a uniform of the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us how many of these MUP in blue uniforms you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I think two or three policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were armed with any weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had automatic rifles and pistols, from what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said you could hear shooting and explosions from the direction of the cultural centre. Did you see any soldiers around the cultural centre, outside the cultural centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: At that point, I didn't see the main entrance to the cultural centre, I couldn't, but the side entrance was where I could see the bodies lying around. I don't recall seeing soldiers around the bodies, but I did hear shooting and explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you go into the coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And tell us what happened in the coffee bar, who you saw, or just continue to --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing happened. When you entered the coffee bar, to the right there was a small room. That's where Brano -- and I can't remember who else, but I know Brano went in, and Franc Kos and I sat -- immediately as you come in to the left, we sat near the door, and they went over there and they talked with the lieutenant-colonel. Not long after that, this person from Bratunac came, the one that I recognised on the photographs here today, that I indicated on the photographs, and he said that everything was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're talking about the person with the bandana on his head?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who, if anyone, did he say, "Everything is finished," to?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He said it. I mean, we could all hear it. I assume that he was addressing the lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was the lieutenant-colonel doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He was sitting there and talking with Brano and the other people. I think they were drinking Sljivovica. I don't know exactly. I think so. And finally at the end, when we were already supposed to leave, because some people wanted to go home, I remember well that the lieutenant-colonel stood up and said, "Who remained alive has remained alive."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what he meant by that or why he said that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Probably I'm thinking of what had happened that day, if somebody, whoever, remained alive, remained alive. That's my opinion. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You have been shown many photographs over the years. Some, you've recognised people, as you've testified to. Have you ever seen a photograph where you have recognised the lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Once I thought I recognised him, and then after considerable thought, I wasn't sure, I couldn't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What happened after the lieutenant-colonel made this comment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to Vlasenica, and when we arrived at the base in Vlasenica, the one that was in Dragosevac, we were told that we should pack and that the Bijeljina platoon was returning to Bijeljina. And that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. McCloskey. On my list, I have all the Defence teams, with the exception of the Gvero Defence team, who wish to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We probably will have some questions later on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. So that changes the scenario straightaway. And for the record, since I previously mentioned that you were not here, Mr. Josse, now I put it on the record that you are present. I have the Popovic Defence team who wish one hour, who would last for one hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we will not cross-examine this witness at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. The Beara, Nikolic and Milotic and Pandurevic teams have each asked for 30 minutes. Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. During the break, I was able to come with my learned friend from the Prosecution, and we're working on a couple of stipulations for the Court and for this case. I'd rather not specifically identify it in front of the witness, with all due respect to him. I think, and I've consulted with several -- or a couple members of our team, if at all possible, with the Court's indulgence, we would like to perhaps start the cross-examination on Monday, and we may short circuit it. We could almost promise that indeed this witness will be completed on Monday, depending again, and I think we're very close to reaching this stipulation with my learned friend, as I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Before we comment on that, is there any -- thank you, Mr. Ostojic -- any other Defence team that is in a position or wishes to start with the cross-examination today? I still have the Borovcanin Defence team have asked for 15 minutes. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We planned for 15 minutes for caution's sake, but in view of the witness's testimony today, we will not be questioning the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. The Nikolic Defence team? This is going to be you or Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be me, Your Honours. I can start with my cross-examination today, and perhaps I can even finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. And then -- I thank you so much, Madam Nikolic. Could you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm going to try today, during this time that we have left, to complete my cross-examination. I would just like to ask you several questions about the soldier with the bandana and about the group that came from Bratunac and joined you at Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, 1995, when you came to Branjevo, already then you saw that man, and his face later appeared in front of the cultural hall and in the coffee bar, so that you managed to actually identify him even ten years later?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not ten years later. I identified him in 1996 when I was here in detention. On television, on British television, the BBC broadcast some footage, and I recognised him then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you already then have information that he was a member of the Panthers Unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you learn about that during meetings with the Prosecutor's office in the course of 2002 and 2004, when you were being interviewed by investigators?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recall having a conversation about the Panthers unit, and I know that that unit was in Bijeljina. They were in the barracks next to ours. We were in one hut and they were in the hut next to us in Bijeljina. I remember that we talked about these people. I'm not sure exactly, but if it says there that we did that, then I agree that we did talk about them then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if, on the 30th of January, 2004, during one of your interviews with the Prosecution, when a series of stills were shown to you of Panther members other than this person, whose name I do not wish to mention in public session, but perhaps the others I can mention in public session since they are not connected to this witness. Gojko Simic, Rajko Tomic, Miodrag Grujicic were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: These names don't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... your microphone. Give me the last couple of lines so that I redact them, please, or block transmission.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the Chamber and to the witness, please. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... exactly your fault entirely, Ms. Nikolic, because the witness jumped straight with his answer before you had even finished. So, Mr. Erdemovic, it's very important that you allow a short pause between question and answer, because otherwise, if there's this overlapping, your voice can be heard, and we are trying to protect you as much as we can. So please observe this golden rule while we proceed. Yes, Madam Nikolic. Perhaps you can repeat your question. Anyway, he has answered it. He says, "These names don't mean anything to me." Your next question, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness please be shown Defence exhibit 1D285. We have the B/C/S and the English version on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Sir, when both versions appear on the screen, could you please look at the second paragraph of this document. It's a report of the Prosecution with the meeting they had with you on the 30th of January, so it's exhibit 1D285 of the 30th of January, 2004. Let me ask you to look at paragraph 2. A sentence in the middle begins: "Of the three of them, the following is known:" Read the text where these three names are mentioned. Do you remember this meeting with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember this document. And as I've already said, these names mean nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I understand, but you remember the meeting and you remember that certain photographs were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you very sincerely, I had too many meetings and I cannot remember every one individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge or have you ever heard that the Panther unit was at that time in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you proceed, Ms. Nikolic. Just for clarity's sake, what we have on the screen is not a transcript of the interview, but an information report, so I think you need to allow for the possibility that parts of the second paragraph that you read out from could be the statement of the person drawing up the information report and not necessarily the statement of the witness. I don't want to call you to any cause, Mr. McCloskey, but I suppose you would agree with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and I think Ms. Nikolic understands that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is a report of the investigator. Maybe I used the wrong word when I tried to describe it, but it is a report of the investigator concerning a meeting with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have only one question to ask of you. Did you have the impression that this soldier with the bandana was, in a way, the leader of that group from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: How shall I put this? I didn't see him issue orders to the others, but he was always around when something was going on. And from the moment when he came up into -- to the lieutenant-colonel in the coffee bar and told him that everything is finished, it was my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What I want to know, given that you saw the photographs from Potocari of a group of soldiers with that man in the bandana, we are speaking of the 12th and 13th July, they were in Potocari, they were in Branjevo on the 16th, they were by the culture hall in Pilica on the 16th, do you know whether Mr. Tomic, Gojko Simic and others were also in other locations where executions were carried out in Zvornik, Orahovac, Kozluk etc.?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I had no knowledge of that. I didn't contact with them at all, and he stuck in my mind because he wore that uniform of the US Army and the bandana, and that's why I remember him but not the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask you one more question concerning the vehicle that the lieutenant-colonel drove in. You testified about that today. You said that it was an Opel Cadet vehicle. On the 6th of November, 1996, the same question was asked of you, and I will, if you don't mind, read that passage from the interview to refresh your memory. You were asked: "What kind of vehicle did the lieutenant-colonel drive?" You answered: "I told you that Opel --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I will have to repeat the question. In fact, I will read that text more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After the question about the vehicle, your answer was: "As for the type, I told you Cadet, the shorter one with a cut-off boot." Your answer was as I just read. The next question asked of you by Jean Rene Ruez is like this: "Coupe, what colour?" And you answered: "Kind of dirty-brownish colour like this bin over here." Did this refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The first thing I said was "Cadet," but that vehicle, when it first appeared in the former Yugoslavia, everybody called it Suza, which means tear, because it had the shape of a tear. I remember that, and I remember pointing at the waste bin that was in the room where I was being questioned, and I meant the drab olive-green-grey colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And the model was coupe?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Opel Cadet.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, sir. I have no further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if it's worth the while of starting another cross-examination, but let me conclude the exercise first. So from Mr. Ostojic, we've heard. Ms. Nikolic has concluded hers. Madame Fauveau, will you be cross-examining this witness? How much time would you require? Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we had envisaged 30 minutes, but in view of the testimony of this witness so far, we will take less. We can start, maybe we can even finish, but I cannot be sure that we will finish before the end of this day. I have just about ten questions, but the length also depends on the answers. It is not certain that I will finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And Mr. Haynes or Mr. Sarapa? I don't know who will be cross-examining this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think it's unlikely we'll have any cross-examination for this witness, but I welcome the opportunity of reflecting upon that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. So, Mr. Petrusic, I suggest you start. Mr. Josse already said that he will be cross-examining, probably, but I don't know whether he wishes to do so today or Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, in fact, is going to do the cross-examination for our team. Fifteen minutes, he tells me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, 15 minutes is too much for today. So I suggest, Mr. Petrusic, you could start now and see where we get or how far we get, and then you'll continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Erdemovic, I appear here for General Miletic in this case, and as I said, I will have only a couple of questions for you. Towards the end of 1993, do you know that in the Territory of the Federation, that is, in the place where you lived, Tuzla, armed conflict was ongoing between the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Croatian Defence Council, the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: End 1993, that's when I moved to Republika Srpska, in November 1993, and I cannot say that there was fighting, but the relations between the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO were very tense. However, conflict had already started in central Bosnia, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In that tense situation, you were arrested by the Croatian Defence Council as you were trying to transport some Serb civilians to the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You told us today that you were first captured -- or rather you were first kept in detention by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then, I quote: "I was moved to a prison held by the HVO."

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I will try to explain the sequence. I was captured on Mount Majevica by the HVO. They took me and one of my colleagues who was accompanying me. They just captured us and held us overnight in their command headquarters, which was on Mount Majevica. And if I remember well, they got orders from the headquarters in Tuzla that the HVO should turn us over for interrogation to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So that coincided with the time when, to say the least, there was pronounced tension between the HVO and the BH Army, if not open conflict?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That's -- that's about it, yes. You could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From what I understand of positions in Majevica, they were held by the HVO at the time.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in one part of Mount Majevica, not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I would now like to move to your involvement in the segment referred to as Srebrenica and your arrival in the area. Those two platoons that arrived, one from Bijeljina and another from Vlasenica, had in total between 30 and 40 men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You have explained that you had four types of uniform. On that day you came to Bijeljina and on to Bratunac and Srebrenica in a black camouflage uniform. What about the rest of the men, the 30 or 40 of them, did they come in the same uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Most of us wore black uniforms, but many others, I cannot tell you exactly how many -- how do I say it? In uniforms of the VRS, and one person that I showed you on the picture, Stanko Savanovic, wore a uniform that we called NATO uniform. It was predominantly the US Army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If I am not mistaken, you designated Stanko Savanovic with number 2 on the photograph shown you by the Prosecutor on 1981. Is he the one you said had an American uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. The person I claim is Stanko Savanovic is number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
